How all product journeys are composed

A source-linked technical walkthrough. Trace the flow, explain the boundary, then test the failure path.

After this session, you can:
  • Distinguish base lifecycle from journey contract
  • Locate journey configuration
  • Read maturity correctly

Technical flow

Every hand-off is a control boundary: on failure the flow holds, refers or denies — it never skips ahead.

  1. 01Base lending lifecycle
  2. 02Product journey contract
  3. 03Tenant configuration
  4. 04Typed workspace
  5. 05Conformance evidence
  6. 06Tenant activation

1. Composition

Every product journey reuses the governed base lifecycle and adds typed facts, evidence gates, lifecycle extensions and product-specific controls. Journey differences are data contracts, not forks of the whole LOS/LMS.

2. Execution

The canonical contract registry defines required fields and evidence. APIs persist tenant journey state, workspaces render typed tasks, and conformance tests cover every declared journey.

3. Maturity

Controlled first slice and configurable pattern describe platform evidence, not a tenant go-live. Each tenant still needs policy bindings, owners, live providers, UAT and operating assurance.
